# git_provider_tool

> Interact with the tenant's configured git provider (GitLab or GitHub) to manage merge requests / pull requests.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | `developer` |
| Callable | MCP clients; in-app @ai conversations; grantable to agents |
| Filter | `https://www.dsiloed.com/api/v1/mcp?tools=git_provider_tool` |

## Description

This is the description the server sends to the model, verbatim.

Interact with the tenant's configured git provider (GitLab or GitHub) to manage
merge requests / pull requests. The tool automatically reads the tenant's dev_team
Configuration to determine which provider and credentials to use.

Operations:
- create_mr: Create a merge/pull request
- list_mrs: List open merge/pull requests
- get_mr: Get details of a specific MR/PR
- update_mr: Update an existing MR/PR's title, description, target branch or assignee
- approve_mr: Approve a MR/PR (manager agents only)
- merge_mr: Merge a MR/PR (manager agents only)
- comment_mr: Add a review comment to a MR/PR
- get_diff: View the diff of a MR/PR

Use project_id to work with a different repo than the default configured one.
project_id must be one of the workspace's registered repositories: an entry in
the dev_team Configuration's repos list (or its top-level project_id when that
list is empty). Any other repo is refused; a workspace admin registers repos.

IMPORTANT: For any operation that takes mr_id (get_mr, get_diff,
approve_mr, merge_mr, comment_mr), pass project_id explicitly. MR
ids are NOT unique across repos — calling get_mr 18 without
project_id will silently use the tenant default and may return a
completely unrelated MR from a different project. The response
includes a `warning` field when project_id was defaulted; if you
see it, retry with project_id set.

EXAMPLES:

Create a merge request:
{operation: "create_mr", source_branch: "feature/sally/signup-validation",
 target_branch: "master", title: "Add signup validation", description: "Adds input validation to signup form"}

List open merge requests:
{operation: "list_mrs"}

List MRs on a different repo:
{operation: "list_mrs", project_id: "russmoniq/PM-Communications-Hub"}

Get MR details:
{operation: "get_mr", mr_id: 42}

Update an MR description (only the fields you pass are changed):
{operation: "update_mr", mr_id: 42, project_id: "model-api/model_api",
 description: "Revised summary covering the latest commits"}

View MR diff:
{operation: "get_diff", mr_id: 42}

Add review comment:
{operation: "comment_mr", mr_id: 42, body: "Looks good, but please add tests for the edge case on line 15"}

Approve and merge:
{operation: "approve_mr", mr_id: 42}
{operation: "merge_mr", mr_id: 42}

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `operation` | string | yes | Git provider operation to perform. One of: `create_mr`, `list_mrs`, `get_mr`, `update_mr`, `approve_mr`, `merge_mr`, `comment_mr`, `get_diff`. |
| `project_id` | string | no | Override the default project ID (e.g. "russmoniq/PM-Communications-Hub"). If not provided, uses the configured default. |
| `source_branch` | string | no | Source branch for the merge request (for create_mr) |
| `target_branch` | string | no | Target branch for the merge request (for create_mr, defaults to configured default_branch; optional for update_mr) |
| `title` | string | no | Title for the merge request (for create_mr; optional for update_mr) |
| `description` | string | no | Description/body for the merge request (for create_mr; optional for update_mr) |
| `assignee` | string | no | Username or ID to assign the MR to (for create_mr; optional for update_mr) |
| `mr_id` | integer | no | Merge request / pull request number (for get_mr, update_mr, approve_mr, merge_mr, comment_mr, get_diff) |
| `body` | string | no | Comment body text (for comment_mr) |
| `state` | string | no | Filter MRs by state (for list_mrs, default: opened) One of: `opened`, `closed`, `merged`, `all`. |
| `squash` | boolean | no | Squash commits when merging (for merge_mr) |
| `delete_branch` | boolean | no | Delete source branch after merge (for merge_mr) |
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | When true, create_mr / merge_mr return the would-be URL and request body WITHOUT POSTing to the git provider (GitLab/GitHub). Other operations (read-only or comment) ignore this flag. Use for eval scenarios or to inspect what an agent would do before letting it mutate. Defaults to false; the response sets `dry_run: true` so callers can distinguish previewed mutations from real ones. |

## Example

```json
{"name": "git_provider_tool", "arguments": {"operation": "get_diff", "project_id": "acme/api", "mr_id": 42}}
```

Returns the merge request's metadata and its diff. Every operation reads the workspace's `dev_team`
Configuration for the provider (`gitlab` / `github`), base URL, default repository, default branch and
the encrypted `git_token`; nothing is passed per call but the operation's own arguments.

## Gotchas

- **Only registered repositories.** `project_id` must be one of the entries in the `dev_team`
  Configuration's `repos` list (or, when that list is empty, its top-level `project_id`); anything
  else — the default repository included, if it is not listed — is refused with
  *"not one of this workspace's registered repositories (the dev_team configuration and its repos
  list)"*. The token usually reaches more (a GitLab group token sees every project in the group),
  so this refusal is the allow-list, not a lookup failure. A workspace admin adds the repository
  under **Administration → Configuration Manager → Configurations → dev_team → repos**; the setup
  is described in the [Git Repositories & Merge Requests](https://www.portablemind.ai/docs/git-repositories)
  guide. The change takes effect on the next call.
- **Pass `project_id` on every call that takes `mr_id`.** MR / PR numbers are only unique within
  one repository. Without `project_id` the call uses the default repository and may return an
  unrelated merge request; the response then carries a `warning` field.
- **`mr_id` is a whole number**, the MR / PR iid, not a URL or a branch name.
- **No `dev_team` Configuration** raises *"No dev_team configuration found for tenant"*: the
  workspace has not connected a git provider yet. Same guide.
- **Approve and merge are for manager roles.** The tool does not stop a developer agent from
  merging; the agent's instructions and the pipeline's human approval gates do. Give `merge_mr` to
  the agent that is meant to have it. `dry_run: true` on `create_mr` / `merge_mr` previews the
  request without sending it.
